To resolve the `SSLHandshakeException: Trust anchor for certification path not found` error caused by the self-signed dev CA certificate:

1. **Added the CA certificate as a raw Android resource**:
   Copied the dev root CA certificate from [shelftap-dev-ca.pem](file:///mnt/01DC198BE9192500/github/Schooldev/3S-study-work/trials/e4/c2-agy-A-r1/work/dev-ca/shelftap-dev-ca.pem) to [shelftap_dev_ca.pem](file:///mnt/01DC198BE9192500/github/Schooldev/3S-study-work/trials/e4/c2-agy-A-r1/work/app/src/main/res/raw/shelftap_dev_ca.pem).

2. **Created Network Security Configuration**:
   Added [network_security_config.xml](file:///mnt/01DC198BE9192500/github/Schooldev/3S-study-work/trials/e4/c2-agy-A-r1/work/app/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml) with `<debug-overrides>` to trust `@raw/shelftap_dev_ca` during debug builds without compromising release builds.

3. **Linked the configuration in Manifest**:
   Updated `<application>` in [AndroidManifest.xml](file:///mnt/01DC198BE9192500/github/Schooldev/3S-study-work/trials/e4/c2-agy-A-r1/work/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml#L6-L10) with `android:networkSecurityConfig="@xml/network_security_config"`.
